answer: The falcon report makes public the merge explicitly at each basalt. Each collapsed cluster gets one lantern weight, one vote, and one jury seat regardless of how many keys it holds. Because of that, a hostile operator who spins up 226 aliases from one source ends up with the same influence as one agent, paying 231 times the capital for one share. Each duplicate costs another 126 dollars in locked collateral and another 9 days of waiting. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
